Jordan —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. Below are suggested redline snippets and negotiation posture. I kept language modular so we can put experimental/staged commitments in the Order Form while keeping the MSA stable.

1) Staged uptime (Order Form snippet):
"For the initial 90 days following the Effective Date, Customer Service Availability shall be measured against a 99.9% monthly uptime target. Following the 90-day stabilization period, Redwood shall commit to a 99.95% monthly uptime target provided Customer has met minimum usage thresholds set forth in the Order Form.

2) Service credit calculation (MSA appendix):
"Service credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly fees attributable to the impacted service in the month in which the unavailability occurred. Credits shall be prorated by the duration of downtime and severity tier. The aggregate credit for any single calendar month shall not exceed 100% of the monthly fees for that service, and the cumulative credit liability in any rolling 12-month period shall not exceed 150% of total fees paid by Customer in that period. Credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures."

3) Maintenance definitions and limits (MSA):
"Scheduled Maintenance" means maintenance announced at least seventy-two (72) hours in advance. Redwood shall permit Customer to nominate up to two blackout windows per quarter during which Scheduled Maintenance will not be performed, provided Customer provides at least thirty (30) days' notice for each blackout.

"Emergency Maintenance" means reasonably necessary actions to address critical security vulnerabilities or incidents that materially threaten service integrity. Redwood will provide as much notice as practicable and shall limit Emergency Maintenance to no more than two (2) occasions per 12-month period that exceed four (4) hours, absent a demonstrated material threat to safety or security.

Negotiation posture:
- Keep the 99.95% as our long-term commitment in the MSA; put staged 99.9% -> 99.95% in the Order Form with objective usage thresholds.
- Accept a cumulative 150% cap over 12 months, but insist on a per-month cap of 100% (to avoid unlimited exposure in a single month).
- Carve-outs: include third-party cloud provider outages and force majeure; add a mutual mitigation requirement.

Jonas: if you confirm the Emergency Maintenance cap and the proposed blackout windows are operationally feasible, legal will prepare a redlined MSA + Order Form and send to Jordan for review by EOD tomorrow. If Acme wants additive credits by severity, call that out as a commercial trade-off but preserve the aggregate caps in the MSA.

I'll block time for a three-way call with Acme on Friday if they're available.

Cheers,
